schemes.eligibility: Displaced person evicted or about to be evicted by Collector/SLAO under land acquisition for NH 17B, including a person unauthorisedly occupying Government land with fixed habitation evicted on account of Four Lane Highway 17B, and in need of shelter; name must be on list prepared by Deputy Collector, Mormugao (published in 3 newspapers, 4 weeks for representations) and finalised by the Board; Board considers economic condition and hardships.
schemes.benefit: Allotment (by lot, in list order) of a shelter of 32 sq. mts. irrespective of area encroached, under an Order of grant; rent fixed per CPWD code for leases to economically weaker sections; Board may in exceptional cases exempt from rent where head of family is a widow or gets Dayanand Social Security Scheme assistance (if that scheme's Government makes matching contribution). Refusal or failure to take possession forfeits rehabilitation rights.
schemes.how_to_apply: No application: Deputy Collector, Mormugao prepares list of displaced persons at Board's request; Member Secretary, Goa Rehabilitation Board, Patto, Panaji intimates allottees.
schemes.later_amendments: 26-03-2012 – Addendum to Goa Rehabilitation Scheme (Rehabilitation of four lane N. H. 17B, project affected persons), 2008
schemes.notes: Gazette Series I No. 7 dated 13-05-2010; issued in supersession of notification dated 03-02-2010; preamble describes it as pre-published draft inviting objections within two weeks. Same gazette pages also carry an unrelated Power Dept post-revival order and draft Land Revenue rules amendment. Fisher-folk shelter of 60.85 sq. mts. added by 2012 addendum.

amendments.name: Addendum to Goa Rehabilitation Scheme (Rehabilitation of four lane N. H. 17B, project affected persons), 2008
amendments.benefit: Inserts para 3(4)(a): Board shall allot to each displaced person from fisher folk community a shelter of 60.85 sq. mts.
amendments.notes: Addendum No. GRB/06/2011-12/107, Official Gazette Series I No. 52 dated 29-03-2012. Rest of page is unrelated Goa Public Service Commission Rules of Procedure, 2012 (not a scheme).

schemes.name: Goa Rehabilitation Scheme, 2007 (victims of landslide)
schemes.target: Families who lost houses in 14 June 1999 Tariwada landslide, Mormugao
schemes.eligibility: Person who lost his house in the landslide of 14th June 1999 at Tariwada, ward No. 3 of Mormugao Municipal Council and who is in need of shelter; name on list prepared by Deputy Collector, Mormugao (published in 3 newspapers, 7 days for representations) and finalised by the Board; Board considers economic condition and hardships.
schemes.benefit: Allotment by lot of a shelter (residential unit) built by the Board on Chalta No. 2 (part), P.T. Sheet No. 52, Sada, Vasco da Gama, under an Order of grant; rent fixed per CPWD code for leases to economically weaker sections; Board may in exceptional cases exempt from rent where head of family is a widow or a Dayanand Social Security Scheme beneficiary (with matching contribution). Not accepting/taking possession forfeits right.
schemes.how_to_apply: No application: list prepared by Deputy Collector, Mormugao at Board's request; Member Secretary of the Board intimates allottees. Map/details at Goa Rehabilitation Board, Patto, Panaji.
schemes.notes: Notification No. GRB/27/07-08/600, Official Gazette Series I No. 45 dated 07-02-2008, notified under Section 35 of the Goa Rehabilitation Board Act, 2006. Shelter size not stated. Same page carries an unrelated HRDF Rules amendment order (Dept of Labour).

schemes.name: Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan (Goa Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan Scheme)
schemes.target: School students, schools and teacher education institutions
schemes.eligibility: Not an individual-application scheme; integrated Centrally Sponsored Scheme (SSA + RMSA + Teacher Education, 2018-19) implemented through a State Implementation Society; preference to Educationally Backward Blocks, LWE, Special Focus Districts, border areas and 115 Aspirational districts.
schemes.benefit: Interventions: universal access incl. infrastructure and retention; gender and equity; inclusive education; quality; teacher salary support; digital initiatives; RTE entitlements incl. uniforms, textbooks; pre-nursery; vocational education; sports and physical education; teacher education/training; monitoring; programme management.
schemes.notes: Overview description only; no amounts, eligibility or application procedure given.

schemes.name: Dayanand Social Security Scheme for Person living with HIV/AIDS
schemes.target: Persons living with HIV/AIDS
schemes.eligibility: 15 years of domicile of Goa; annual income below Rs 24000.
schemes.benefit: Rs 2000 per month as social security.
schemes.how_to_apply: Form from nearest ART centre, Goa State AIDS Control Society or Social Welfare Department; submit to Goa State AIDS Control Society.
schemes.notes: Amount is per month. Beneficiaries stated: 406.

schemes.name: Free Travel in Kadamba Buses in Entire Goa State (Kadamba Bus pass for PLHIV)
schemes.target: Persons living with HIV/AIDS
schemes.eligibility: Person living with HIV taking treatment in ART Centres of Goa; residence proof of Goa.
schemes.benefit: Free bus travel in Kadamba buses across Goa.
schemes.how_to_apply: Get form from nearest ART centre or Goa State AIDS Control Society.
schemes.notes: Total beneficiaries stated: 1700.

schemes.name: Goa State Library (Financial Assistance) Amendment Rules, 2004 - Grant-in-aid to Libraries run by Non-Government Institutions (Panchayat / Village Libraries)
schemes.target: Panchayat / village libraries
schemes.eligibility: Village/panchayat libraries receiving grants under old pattern, fulfilling conditions; Gram Panchayat, NGO (registered with State Government Authority, with registered/approved library management rules) or Municipality managing a public library; independent premises of about 40 sq. mts. with lighting/ventilation; maintain prescribed registers (accession, accounts, issue, members, visitors, dead stock etc.); timings: taluka libraries min 6.5 hrs, panchayat libraries min 6 hrs on working days, 6-day week; open to inspection/audit; annual report by 30th May and CA-audited accounts by 30th/31st October; separate bank account in library's name; undertaking to hand over Government-funded materials on withdrawal of grant.
schemes.benefit: (i) Manpower remuneration (max 2 persons) up to maximum Rs.60,000/- or actual expenditure, whichever is less; (ii) 100% assistance on admissible items other than manpower, subject to maximum Rs.60,000/-.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application in prescribed form (Annexure-I) to the State Library Officer (available with Directorate of Education, Panaji).
schemes.notes: Notification No. 27-273-03/DE/AE/678, supersedes notification dated 21-3-2003. Grant released in two equal instalments (after annual report by 31st May; after CA-audited accounts by 31st October). Grants can be withheld/recovered for non-compliance. Admissible items: staff pay, rent (certified by PWD EE), minor repairs, books/periodicals, printing, furniture/equipment, insurance, contingencies, events (World Book Day, Librarian Day, National Book Week).

schemes.name: Goa State Library (Financial Assistance) Amendment Rules, 2004 - Grant-in-aid to Libraries run by Non-Government Institutions (Taluka Libraries)
schemes.target: Taluka libraries run by non-Government institutions/municipalities
schemes.eligibility: Taluka libraries that have been receiving grants under old pattern; Gram Panchayat, NGO (registered with State Government Authority, with registered/approved library management rules) or Municipality managing a public library; independent premises of about 40 sq. mts. with lighting/ventilation; maintain prescribed registers (accession, accounts, issue, members, visitors, dead stock etc.); timings: taluka libraries min 6.5 hrs, panchayat libraries min 6 hrs on working days, 6-day week; open to inspection/audit; annual report by 30th May and CA-audited accounts by 30th/31st October; separate bank account in library's name; undertaking to hand over Government-funded materials on withdrawal of grant.
schemes.benefit: (i) Manpower remuneration (max 3 persons) up to maximum Rs.1.20 lakhs or actual expenditure, whichever is less; (ii) 100% assistance on admissible items other than manpower, subject to maximum Rs.1.50 lakhs.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application in prescribed form (Annexure-I) to the State Library Officer (available with Directorate of Education, Panaji).
schemes.notes: Notification No. 27-273-03/DE/AE/678, supersedes notification dated 21-3-2003. Grant released in two equal instalments (after annual report by 31st May; after CA-audited accounts by 31st October). Grants can be withheld/recovered for non-compliance. Admissible items: staff pay, rent (certified by PWD EE), minor repairs, books/periodicals, printing, furniture/equipment, insurance, contingencies, events (World Book Day, Librarian Day, National Book Week). Max = larger of the two separate caps (Rs.1.20 lakh manpower + Rs.1.50 lakh items).

schemes.name: Goa State Library (Financial Assistance) Amendment Rules, 2004 - Grant-in-aid to Libraries run by Non-Government Institutions (Token Grant for new public libraries)
schemes.target: Applicants proposing to open new public libraries
schemes.eligibility: Proposal for opening a new public library; applicant/management/NGO fulfils Department's conditions for opening public libraries and submits financial statement/bank account details to Director of Education; Gram Panchayat, NGO (registered with State Government Authority, with registered/approved library management rules) or Municipality managing a public library; independent premises of about 40 sq. mts. with lighting/ventilation; maintain prescribed registers (accession, accounts, issue, members, visitors, dead stock etc.); timings: taluka libraries min 6.5 hrs, panchayat libraries min 6 hrs on working days, 6-day week; open to inspection/audit; annual report by 30th May and CA-audited accounts by 30th/31st October; separate bank account in library's name; undertaking to hand over Government-funded materials on withdrawal of grant.
schemes.benefit: Token grant of Rs.50,000/-.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application in prescribed form (Annexure-I) to the State Library Officer (available with Directorate of Education, Panaji).
schemes.notes: Notification No. 27-273-03/DE/AE/678, supersedes notification dated 21-3-2003. Grant released in two equal instalments (after annual report by 31st May; after CA-audited accounts by 31st October). Grants can be withheld/recovered for non-compliance. Admissible items: staff pay, rent (certified by PWD EE), minor repairs, books/periodicals, printing, furniture/equipment, insurance, contingencies, events (World Book Day, Librarian Day, National Book Week).

schemes.name: Government Intervention for Control of Price Rise Scheme, 2014
schemes.target: Goan consumers (residents of Goa)
schemes.eligibility: Consumer who is a resident of Goa; subsidised food commodities on production of ration card at specified outlets; vegetables at Goa State Horticultural Corporation Ltd. outlets.
schemes.benefit: Subsidy at point of purchase: select food commodities at subsidised rates, maximum 2 kgs per month per card each (e.g. white peas (vatana), green grams (moong); wheat flour (atta) 4 kgs per month per card); 10 vegetables (bhendi, cabbage, carrot, cauliflower, cluster beans, French beans, green chillies, onion, potato, tomato) at subsidised rates, max 2 kgs of each item per person per day, incl. via mobile vans. GSHCL reimbursed 25% of procurement value of vegetables, 5% margin on commodities, and up to Rs.3000/- per day per mobile van (max 25 days/month, ~20 vans).
schemes.how_to_apply: Purchase at GSHCL outlets / mobile vans; ration card required for commodities.
schemes.valid_period: From 10-02-2014 until withdrawn
schemes.notes: Notification No. 3/2/HS/44/GICPR/2013-14/DIR.AGRI/664 (Directorate of Agriculture). OCR heavily damaged: list of commodities partly lost; subsidy rates not legible. Budget cap Rs. 20 crores (produce/commodities) and Rs. 1.8 crores (mobile vans). Monitoring committee under Director of Agriculture; grievances to Minister for Agriculture. Concurrence Finance U.O. dated 30/10/2013.

schemes.name: Promotion of [vegetable cultivation through] Assured Markets, 2015-16
schemes.target: Vegetable cultivators registered with GSHCL
schemes.eligibility: Registered farmers growing identified commercial vegetables (onion, tomato, bhendi, green chilly, cluster bean, cucumber, ridge gourd, bitter gourd, tendli, bottle gourd (trellis grown), brinjal, elephant foot yam, ginger); must intimate probable quantity to GSHCL 2 days in advance via supervisors at procurement centres; produce must meet quality standards and be within eligible quantity for area grown.
schemes.benefit: Assured purchase by GSHCL at procurement centres/collection points at pre-fixed price (base price = average approved supply price for corresponding fortnight of previous year, plus additional amount of Rs.8) or approved supplier's rate for the day, whichever is higher. GSHCL reimbursed from scheme funds for procurement centre rent/infrastructure, sorting/grading centres, vehicle hire, and additional 10% of total purchase value for losses (driage, spoilage).
schemes.how_to_apply: Register with Goa State Horticultural Corporation Ltd.; supply at its procurement centres (18 existing) or designated collection points.
schemes.valid_period: From 1st April 2015 until withdrawn or amended
schemes.notes: OCR badly damaged: exact scheme title partly lost ('Promotion 0 : Assured Markets'); unit for the Rs.8 addition (likely per kg) not legible. Finance concurrence U.O. dated 17/02/2016. Directorate of Agriculture to supply seed of identified varieties under its schemes. First pages are annexure forms of the 2014 price-rise scheme (Part I).

schemes.name: Ashraya Adhar Scheme
schemes.department: Goa State Scheduled Tribes Finance And Development Corporation Ltd.
schemes.target: Scheduled Tribe house owners needing repair/renovation/reconstruction
schemes.eligibility: Any person of ST Community owning a house (incl. mundcarial house) individually or jointly; each separately residing family unit in jointly owned house eligible; age not more than 55 years on date of application (58 for employees of State/Central Govt/Govt Corporation/Board/aided institute). After closing a loan, beneficiary/family member may get a further loan up to Rs.5,00,000/- provided active loan per family per house does not exceed Rs.5 lakhs (101st BOD meeting 5-2-2025).
schemes.benefit: Loan up to Rs. 5,00,000/- at 2% interest per annum, repayment 10 years incl. 3 months moratorium (re-fixed to age 60 if applicant above 50; to retirement + 6 months for Govt employees); disbursed 75% as 1st instalment and 25% after utilisation bills, photos and inspection.
schemes.how_to_apply: Separate application forms at Panaji and Margao corporation offices. Documents: ST certificate, 2 photos, age proof, Aadhar, bank mandate/passbook, latest house tax receipt, self affidavit and co-owner NOC on Rs.100/- stamp paper (notarised), estimate cost of repair, photos of house, income proof (salary certificate/income affidavit/pay slip/3 years ITR), Form 16 or 3 months bank statement, documents of 2 sureties (one surety enough if Govt employee; none if applicant is Govt employee).
schemes.notes: Summary document (posted 2025). Loan, not grant; recovered as land revenue arrears if unpaid.

schemes.name: Self Employment Scheme
schemes.department: Goa State Scheduled Tribes Finance And Development Corporation Ltd.
schemes.target: Unemployed ST persons and ST-only groups/societies for self-employment
schemes.eligibility: Unemployed person belonging to ST Community, age not more than 55 years (relaxable by BOD). Annual family income not exceeding Rs. 3,00,000/- (relaxable in deserving cases). Associations/Societies/Partnerships/SHGs/Companies formed exclusively by ST members also eligible. Two guarantors/sureties, one necessarily a Government servant. Activities excluded: dealing in alcohol, fire crackers and tobacco.
schemes.benefit: Loan up to Rs. 10 lakh to an unemployed individual and up to Rs. 15 lakhs to Association/Society/Partnership/SHG/Company of ST members, at 4% interest per annum (reducing balance), repayment up to 10 years as decided by BOD; beneficiary contributes 10% margin money (relaxable by BOD for individuals only); 2% penal interest on overdue.
schemes.how_to_apply: Prescribed application form with ST certificate, 2 photos, family income certificate, ration card, age proof, Aadhar, self-declaration affidavit, surety salary certificate and affidavit on Rs.100 stamp paper, plus sector-specific documents (land title/I & XIV form for agriculture; NOC from Panchayat/Municipality, viability report, quotations for allied/manufacturing/trade; project report, quotation, driving licence for vehicles). Approved by Board of Directors, sanctioned by MD. Business mortgaged to Corporation; insurance required. Forms at Panaji and Margao corporation offices.
schemes.notes: Loan, not grant. Max is for groups/societies (Rs. 10 lakh for individuals).

schemes.name: Short Term Loan Scheme
schemes.department: Goa State Scheduled Tribes Finance And Development Corporation Ltd.
schemes.target: Scheduled Tribe individuals/students of Goa
schemes.eligibility: Any individual from ST community of State of Goa; may reapply only after clearing earlier loan under the scheme.
schemes.benefit: Short term loan up to Rs. 1,00,000/- for education, medical or business purposes; education loan at interest rate of 2% per annum (repayment period per clause 7(f), later 20 months); 1% penal interest on overdue instalments.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply in prescribed form to Goa State Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation Ltd. with ST certificate, bank passbook copy with photo, salary certificate/pay slip of one surety with affidavit on Rs. 50/- stamp paper, photo and ID proof of surety, Aadhar copy, affidavit on Rs. 50/- stamp paper on loan amount and purpose (parent/guardian if under 18). Sub-committee of 3 directors sanctions; agreement on Rs. 50 stamp paper.
schemes.valid_period: Five years from date of issue
schemes.notes: Notification No. 1-288(7)/2018-19/ADMN/DTW/346 (Director of Tribal Welfare), gazette dated 14th June 2018. OCR damaged in clause 7(f) (repayment terms; appears 10 months/10 instalments). Concurrence Finance U.O. dated 25-05-2018. Loan amount, not grant.

schemes.name: Short Term Loan Scheme for Education, Medical and Business Purpose
schemes.department: Goa State Scheduled Tribes Finance And Development Corporation Ltd.
schemes.target: ST individuals/students of Goa
schemes.eligibility: Any individual from ST community of State of Goa; may reapply after clearing earlier loan.
schemes.benefit: Short term loan up to Rs. 1,00,000/- for business, education or medical purpose at 2% per annum: education loan repayable within 20 months (max 20 instalments), business/medical within 10 months (max 10 instalments), each with 3-month moratorium; 1% penal interest on overdue.
schemes.how_to_apply: Prescribed application form to GSSTFDCL with ST certificate, bank passbook copy with photo, surety salary certificate/pay slip with affidavit on Rs.100/- stamp paper, photo and ID proof, Aadhar, applicant affidavit on Rs.100/- stamp paper on amount and purpose (parent/guardian if under 18). Sub-committee sanctions; agreement on Rs.50 stamp paper. Forms at Panaji and Margao offices.
schemes.notes: Loan, not grant.

schemes.name: Short Term Loans to Hawkers / Vendors
schemes.department: Goa State Scheduled Tribes Finance And Development Corporation Ltd.
schemes.target: Scheduled Tribe vegetable/flower/fruit cultivators, vegetable and fish vendors, hawkers
schemes.eligibility: Individual belonging to Scheduled Tribe community engaged in vegetable production, flower or fruit cultivation, vegetable vending, fish vending or hawking, facing difficulty getting finance.
schemes.benefit: Loan of Rs. 2,000/- to Rs. 5,000/- at 2% interest per annum, repayable in maximum 10 instalments; 1% penal interest on overdue.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application form to Goa State ST Finance & Development Corporation Ltd., 2nd Floor, Dayanand Smriti Building, Swami Vivekanand Road, Panaji, with Samaj/ST certificate, promissory note for 10 instalments, identity proof (election card/bank passbook with photo), agreement on Rs. 5 stamp paper.

schemes.name: Scheme of Family Counselling Centre
schemes.target: Voluntary organisations running Family Counselling Centres for women and children in distress
schemes.eligibility: Organisation registered under appropriate Act (or regular branch of a registered body); registered on NITI Aayog portal with UID, PAN and office bearers' Aadhaar/PAN; engaged in social welfare work for at least 3 years (relaxable for hilly/remote/border/tribal areas, specialised or new services); properly constituted managing committee with adequate female members, members not related to each other; sound finances; open to all citizens without discrimination; no other grant for same purpose; no fee charged to beneficiaries.
schemes.benefit: Revised budget: honorarium of two counsellors @ Rs.10,000/- p.m. each (Rs. 2,40,000/-); rent @ Rs. 3000/- p.m. and contingencies @ Rs. 44,000/- per annum (Rs. 80,000/-); total Rs. 3,20,000/-; 90% contribution by CSWB i.e. Rs. 2,88,000/- per annum, 10% matching by VO i.e. Rs. 32,000/- per annum.
schemes.how_to_apply: Proposal with budget submitted through the State Social Welfare Board; examined on merit.
schemes.notes: Central Social Welfare Board scheme (1983). Rs. 2,88,000 is CSWB's annual grant per centre. Rent stated as Rs. 3000 p.m. here vs Rs. 36000 p.a. in doc ab50e53042 (equivalent).

schemes.name: Financial Assistance / Scholarships, Awards & Other Schemes of Assistance (Government College of Commerce & Economics, Borda, Margao)
schemes.target: Students of Government College of Commerce & Economics, Margao
schemes.eligibility: College merit scholarships: first 3 students in each class per term with at least 60% marks (Term 1 on previous year's exam, Term 2 on First Term exam). Post Matric Scholarship to SC/OBC: SC/OBC students specified in relation to Goa who passed last qualifying exam; only one student per family. Scholarships to handicapped students: minimum 40% disability. Merit scholarship to children of school teachers: first class at SSC (March/April) and parent's income less than Rs. 25000/- per annum after standard deduction.
schemes.benefit: Class-wise prizes, sponsored cash prizes; 1st ranker Certificate of Merit and cash prize of Rs. 1500/-; highest marks in Financial Accounting (T.Y. B.Com Sem VI) Certificate of Merit and cash prize Rs 1000/-; merit scholarships; facilitation of government scholarships (Rajiv Gandhi Shiksha Sahaya Yojana, Post Matric SC/OBC, handicapped, Gagan Bharari Shiksha Yojana for ST, Minority post matric, Dayanand Bandodkar scheme for orphans, Goa Financial Assistance towards fees 2014, freeships for children of freedom fighters/service personnel/mine workers/armed forces, national loan scholarship, bank loans).
schemes.how_to_apply: Details displayed on college notice board from time to time.
schemes.notes: Compilation/list of awards and government scholarships available at the college; amounts of government scholarships not stated.

schemes.name: Providing free Laptops to meritorious students belonging to Schedule Tribe (ST) and Schedule Caste (SC) Communities
schemes.department: Info Tech Corporation of Goa Ltd
schemes.target: Top Class X ST and SC students in each taluka, academic year 2022-23
schemes.eligibility: Class X students of academic year 2022-23 belonging to ST or SC communities; top 10 meritorious ST students (5 boys, 5 girls) and top 10 SC students (5 boys, 5 girls) per taluka in Goa; subject to document verification.
schemes.benefit: Free laptop.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply online at https://infotech.goa.gov.in; last date 05/10/2023; subject to document verification.
schemes.valid_period: Academic year 2022-23; applications till 05-10-2023
schemes.notes: Implemented by DITE&C through ITG. Funding inferred as State department (DITE&C) - not explicitly stated.

schemes.name: Community Development Through Polytechnics (formerly Scheme of Community Polytechnic Wing)
schemes.target: Dropout students, unemployed youth, women, rural masses and slum dwellers in Vasco, Mormugao, Cortalim, Marcaim, Priol & St Andrez areas
schemes.benefit: Free skill development training courses of 03 to 06 months (technical: welding, machinist, carpentry, PCB, computer, Tally, typewriting, office assistant, AC & refrigeration, diesel mechanic, computer hardware; non-technical: tailoring, embroidery, macrame, crochet, flower making, beautician, sea shell and coconut handicrafts); awareness programmes, technical support services; exhibition-cum-sale opportunity.
schemes.how_to_apply: Training at the Institute and its extension centres in villages.
schemes.notes: Descriptive background of a Government of India (Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship) scheme implemented since April 1991; OCR text. Awareness programmes held in panchayat premises but no formal local body role. Funding implicitly central but not stated.

schemes.name: Advance for Purchase or Construction of House
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Fund members purchasing or constructing a house
schemes.eligibility: Member of the Fund; advance not sanctioned to those who do not have continuous membership in the Fund for five years and fifteen years service left for superannuation (as far as legible); completion certificate within six months of withdrawal.
schemes.benefit: Advance not exceeding fifty thousand rupees for outright purchase of a house or construction of house, recovered in equal instalments fixed by the Board.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application in Form No. XXIX with approved plan and estimate, 14-year encumbrance certificate, location certificate, land tax receipt, title documents, ration card, identity card and passbook, title clearance, NOC from authorities for construction, declaration of not owning a house.
schemes.notes: Heavily garbled OCR; eligibility condition (2) reconstructed from broken text and may be inaccurate. Form also mentions maintenance and purchase of land with building.

schemes.name: Death Benefit
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Nominees/dependents of deceased Fund members
schemes.eligibility: Nominee/dependent of a member who dies; higher amount where death is due to accident during the course of employment.
schemes.benefit: Fifty thousand rupees for natural death; One Lakh rupees if death is due to an accident during the course of employment.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application in Form No. XXXVII to the Secretary or authorised officer with death/accident death certificate from Government doctor not below Assistant Surgeon rank and other specified documents; appeal to Board within sixty days.
schemes.notes: Fragmented text layer but amounts legible.

schemes.name: Disability Pension
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Fund beneficiaries permanently disabled by paralysis, leprosy, TB, accident etc.
schemes.eligibility: Beneficiary (registered member) permanently disabled due to paralysis, leprosy, TB, accident etc.; conditions fixed by the Board.
schemes.benefit: Disability pension of one hundred and fifty rupees per mensem, plus ex-gratia payment of not more than five thousand rupees depending upon percentage of disability.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application in Form No. XXXIX (rule 280(2)) with certificates, medical bills and documents specified by the Board.
schemes.notes: Rs. 5,000 is the one-time ex-gratia; pension is Rs. 150 per month.

schemes.name: Family Pension
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Surviving spouse of a deceased pensioner (welfare Fund member)
schemes.eligibility: Surviving spouse of a deceased pensioner; application within three months of the pensioner's death.
schemes.benefit: Family pension of fifty percent of the pension received by the pensioner or one hundred rupees, whichever is higher.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application in Form No. XLV (rule 288) within three months of death, with death certificate of worker and Village Officer's certificates of relationship, not receiving pension, and not receiving salary from Government/Semi-Government/Private institution.
schemes.notes: Monthly amount; minimum Rs. 100. 'Village Officer' certificates are a document requirement (revenue official, not a local body).

schemes.name: Financial Assistance for Education
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Children of welfare Fund members pursuing courses specified by the Board
schemes.eligibility: Children of members of the Fund, for courses of study specified by the Board.
schemes.benefit: Financial assistance as may be determined by the Board.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application in Form No. XLIII (rule 286) within time specified by the Board, with qualifying exam marks, parent's affidavit (signed before MLA/MP/Panchayat President/Gazetted Officer) and certificate from head of institution.
schemes.notes: No amounts stated. Panchayat President only one of alternative attesting authorities.

schemes.name: Financial Assistance for Marriage
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Building workers (Fund members) for marriage of children or own marriage (women members)
schemes.eligibility: Building workers with continuous membership for three years; for marriage of their children (up to two children) or a female member's own marriage.
schemes.benefit: Financial assistance of two thousand rupees per marriage, for the marriage of two children of the beneficiary.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application in Form No. XLIV (rule 287) with marriage certificate and other documents specified by the Board.
schemes.notes: Portal title mentions 'Pension Benefit' but document is only marriage assistance.

schemes.name: Funeral Assistance
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Nominees/dependents of deceased Fund members
schemes.eligibility: Nominee/dependent of a deceased member of the Fund (live membership); non-nominee must submit dependence certificate.
schemes.benefit: Ten thousand rupees towards funeral expenses.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application in Form No. XLI (rule 282) with membership/subscription details, nominee consent letters and guardianship certificate where applicable.
schemes.notes: Board not named (likely construction workers welfare board).

schemes.name: Grant for the Purchase of Tools
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Members of the welfare Fund needing tools
schemes.eligibility: Members who have completed three years membership in the Fund and remit contribution regularly; not completed fifty-five years of age.
schemes.benefit: Grant of five thousand rupees for the purchase of tools.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application in Form No. XL (rule 281) with invoice of instruments, salary/employment certificate and other documents specified by the Board.
schemes.notes: Board not named in text (likely construction workers welfare board).

schemes.name: Interim Relief to the Beneficiaries Affected by Disaster
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Beneficiaries affected by disaster, catastrophes or natural calamities
schemes.eligibility: Beneficiaries affected by disaster, catastrophes or natural calamities; employee/worker possessing beneficiary card; committee decides modalities, quantum and procedure.
schemes.benefit: Upto an amount of Rs. 10,00,000/-
schemes.how_to_apply: Beneficiary card
schemes.notes: Summary table of BOCW (building & other construction workers welfare) schemes; URL indicates dated 08-09-2015 (not printed in text). Amounts differ from the separate rule-text documents posted 2020 (fe3a453a06 etc.). Rs. 10 lakh is aggregate ceiling for the affected area per rule 288A, not per beneficiary.

schemes.name: Interim Relief to the Beneficiaries Affected by Disaster (Rule 288A)
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Registered beneficiaries affected by disaster, catastrophes or natural calamities
schemes.eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries of the affected area affected by disaster, catastrophe or natural calamity, pending disbursement of benefits under approved schemes.
schemes.benefit: Immediate relief up to an amount of Rupees ten lakhs among all eligible beneficiaries of the affected area, including cash payment and expenditure on facilities and benefits; quantum and modalities decided by committee (Minister (Labour) chairman, Secretary (Labour), Commissioner Labour and Employment).
schemes.notes: Single rule text (288A) inserted into welfare rules; the Rs. 10 lakh is an aggregate ceiling across all beneficiaries of an area, not per beneficiary. Board/rules not named in text (likely construction workers welfare rules).

schemes.name: Loan for the Purchase of Tools
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Registered construction workers
schemes.eligibility: Beneficiary who has completed 3 yrs membership in the fund and remits regular contribution.
schemes.how_to_apply: Form No. XL
schemes.notes: Summary table of BOCW (building & other construction workers welfare) schemes; URL indicates dated 08-09-2015 (not printed in text). Amounts differ from the separate rule-text documents posted 2020 (fe3a453a06 etc.). Called 'loan' here but 'grant' in rule text (e3aee7f2c7).

schemes.name: Maternity Benefit
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Registered women workers (members of welfare Fund) on confinement
schemes.eligibility: Registered member paying subscription; pregnant/delivered (medical certificate required).
schemes.how_to_apply: Application in Form XXXIV (rule 276) with copy of challans or pass book and original medical certificate from a Medical Officer not below the rank of Assistant Surgeon.
schemes.notes: Document contains only the application form and medical certificate; benefit amount and rule text not included. OCR partly garbled.

schemes.name: Medical Assistance
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Registered construction workers hospitalised
schemes.eligibility: Beneficiary hospitalised for 5 or more days due to accident or any disease.
schemes.benefit: Rs.400/- for first 5 days hospitalised and Rs.40/- for remaining days, subject to maximum Rs. 2000/-
schemes.how_to_apply: Form No. XLII or XLVI
schemes.notes: Summary table of BOCW (building & other construction workers welfare) schemes; URL indicates dated 08-09-2015 (not printed in text). Amounts differ from the separate rule-text documents posted 2020 (fe3a453a06 etc.).

schemes.name: Medical Assistance - disability due to accident
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Registered workers disabled due to accident
schemes.eligibility: Registered worker who suffers disability as a result of an accident.
schemes.benefit: Financial assistance up to a maximum of five thousand rupees depending upon the percentage of disability.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application in Form XLVI (ex-gratia medical assistance for accidents, rule 285) with documents specified by the Board.
schemes.notes: Same document as hospitalisation component.

schemes.name: Medical Assistance - hospitalisation
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Registered beneficiaries hospitalised due to accident or disease
schemes.eligibility: Registered beneficiary (subscription-paying) hospitalised for five or more days due to accident or any disease, or met with accident and put in plaster at residence.
schemes.benefit: Rs. 400 ("400 hundred rupees") for the first five days and twenty rupees each for remaining days, subject to a maximum one thousand rupees.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application in Form no. XLII (application for medical benefit) with documents specified by the Board.
schemes.notes: Text reads '400 hundred rupees' (likely Rs. 400). Board not named; forms refer to registration no. and subscriptions (likely a welfare board for registered workers). Partly OCR-garbled form headers.

schemes.name: Pension
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Building workers who are members of the welfare Fund, on reaching 60 years
schemes.eligibility: Member of the Fund who has been working as a building worker for not less than one year after the commencement of these rules, on completion of sixty years of age.
schemes.benefit: Pension of one hundred and fifty rupees per mensem, plus increase of ten rupees for every completed year of service beyond five years; payable from first day of month succeeding the month of completing 60 years; Board may revise with Government approval.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application in Form No. XXXV to the Secretary of the Board or authorised officer with identity card, pass book and challans; appeal to Board within sixty days of rejection.
schemes.notes: Monthly base amount (Rs. 150/month; increments extra). Heavily fragmented OCR/text layer; content reconstructed from broken word order. Board not named but text refers to building workers (likely Goa Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board rules).

schemes.name: Pension Benefit
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Construction workers (Fund members)
schemes.eligibility: Member of the fund who is working not less than 1 year.
schemes.benefit: Rs. 300/- per mensem and an increase of Rs.10/- for every completed year of service beyond 5 yrs.
schemes.how_to_apply: Form No. XXXV
schemes.notes: Summary table of BOCW (building & other construction workers welfare) schemes; URL indicates dated 08-09-2015 (not printed in text). Amounts differ from the separate rule-text documents posted 2020 (fe3a453a06 etc.). Monthly amount; age condition (60 years) appears only in rule text a05cfa096a.

schemes.name: Scheme II - Grant of Financial Assistance to the School Going Children of Industrial Workers/Employees Studying in 1st to 4th Standard for Supply of One Set of Uniform
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Children (Std 1-4) of industrial workers/employees
schemes.eligibility: Industrial worker/employee with at least 6 months continuous service; salary not exceeding Rs.20,000/- per month; child studying in 1st to 4th standard in recognised, aided or private schools (children in Government schools already supplied uniforms are not eligible); selection by lowest parental income and lowest age (5-10 years); preference to workers with not more than two children.
schemes.benefit: Rs.1600/- per student per annum towards purchase of one set of uniform.
schemes.how_to_apply: Prescribed form through employer or school to the Secretary, Goa Labour Welfare Board, Shram Shakti Bhavan, 4th Floor, Patto Plaza, Panaji, on or before 30th September, with employer certificate and institution certificate.

schemes.name: Scheme III - Scheme for Award of Scholarships to School or College going Children of Employees / Industrial Employees in Various Establishments
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: School/college-going children of industrial workers in establishments covered by the Goa, Daman & Diu Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1986
schemes.eligibility: Parent is a regular worker (min. 6 months continuous service) in a covered industrial establishment doing skilled/unskilled, manual or clerical work (not supervisory/managerial); salary not exceeding Rs. 20,000/- per month including allowances excluding bonus; student admitted to recognised institution in India; not repeating same stage in different subject or switching professional line (research/higher study in same line allowed); 'Lower Category' (income from all sources up to Rs. 3,500/- per month, OBC, physically handicapped children - 10% reservation) must have qualified for promotion; others need 45% or more aggregate in last annual exam; merit is primary consideration; other scholarships reduce award to the excess amount.
schemes.benefit: Scholarship per student per year: Group I (Class V & VI) Rs. 2000/-; Group II (Class VII-X) Rs. 2800/-; Group III (Class XI, XII etc., pre-graduation) Rs. 3600/-; Group IV (graduation/post-graduation in Arts, Science, Commerce and lower technical like B.T., L.T., B.Ed., M.Ed., LL.B.) Rs. 10,000/-; Group V (M.B.B.S., B.E., B.Sc. (Agri.), higher technical, research and doctorate) Rs. 20,000/-; paid in one instalment via ECS to parent's bank account.
schemes.how_to_apply: Prescribed form (Schedule III) sent to the Secretary, Goa Labour Welfare Board through the Head of the Institution, with employer certificate (Part II) of employment and income (two if both parents employed) and institution certificate; last date 30th September each year.
schemes.notes: Number of scholarships fixed annually by Board Secretary subject to funds (max 10% increase over previous year). Rs. 20,000 is per year.

schemes.name: Scheme IV - Scheme for Supply of T.V. Sets to Industrial Establishments/Labour Welfare Centres/Clubs/Recreation Rooms
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Industrial establishments, Government Labour Welfare Centres, and clubs/recreation rooms of registered trade unions
schemes.eligibility: Industrial establishments, Labour Welfare Centres run by Government of Goa, and clubs/recreation rooms run by registered trade unions with minimum 300 worker members; preference to labour-concentrated areas; agreement to maintain set and exhibit programmes daily, bear incidental expenses and provide accommodation; not more than one TV set per establishment.
schemes.benefit: Colour T.V. set purchased by Welfare Fund, cost including accessories not exceeding Rs. 25,000/-; or full reimbursement for Black and White T.V. set subject to maximum Rs. 12,000/-.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application form in triplicate signed by manager with seal to Goa Labour Welfare Board; execute bond/agreement.

schemes.name: Scheme IX - Creches: Scheme for the Benefit of Children of Industrial Workers/Employees
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Industrial workers with children aged 1-3 years in creches
schemes.eligibility: Children of industrial workers aged 1 to 3 years; parents' monthly income not exceeding Rs. 20,000/-; not for parents already getting creche facility under labour laws; child enrolled in private creche in locality or at workplace; employer certificate of over 6 months continuous service and establishment covered under Goa, Daman & Diu Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1986.
schemes.benefit: Reimbursement of creche fees on matching basis on production of receipt, subject to a maximum of Rs. 2,000/- per month.
schemes.how_to_apply: Prescribed form through employer to the Secretary, Goa Labour Welfare Board, Shram Shakti Bhavan, Patto Plaza, Panjim, with child's birth certificate attested by Gazetted officer, employer certificate (Part II) and creche certificate (Part III).
schemes.notes: Max benefit is per month.

schemes.name: Scheme No. I - Grant of Financial Assistance for Purchase of Text Books / Note Books to School Going Children of Industrial Workers/Employees
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Children (Class I-IV) of industrial workers/employees
schemes.eligibility: Children of regular industrial workers/employees with at least 6 months continuous service; supervisory/managerial staff drawing Rs. 1600/- and above per month excluded; wages/salary not exceeding Rs. 20,000/-; child studying in class I to IV in recognised/approved school; those supplied slates/text books/note books by Government of Goa not entitled; selection by lowest parental income, preference to higher classes, priority to workers with not more than two children.
schemes.benefit: Class I Rs. 1200.00; Class II Rs. 1200.00; Class III Rs. 1800.00; Class IV Rs. 1800.00 for purchase of text books/note books, disbursed through the Head of Institution.
schemes.how_to_apply: Prescribed form through employer or Head of Educational Institution to the Secretary, Goa Labour Welfare Board, Shram Shakti Bhavan, 4th Floor, Patto Plaza, Panaji, on or before 30th September every year.

schemes.name: Scheme No. V - Scheme for Grant of Financial Assistance to the Industrial Workers/Employee for Purchase of Spectacles
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Industrial workers/employees needing spectacles
schemes.eligibility: Industrial workers/employees with one year of service (broken spells counted) on date of application, covered under clause (c) of Section 2 of Goa, Daman and Diu Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1986; eyes tested at State hospital, GMC or qualified optician; no replacement within 5 years.
schemes.benefit: Reimbursement of cost of frame and lenses up to Rs.2000/- (excess borne by worker); lens replacement after one year if power changes, at cost not exceeding Rs.400/-.
schemes.how_to_apply: Prescribed form to the Secretary, Goa Labour Welfare Board with cash receipt, prescription from optician/doctor, management/contractor certificate of service and wages, and medical officer/eye specialist certificates.

schemes.name: Scheme No. VI - Child Care Benefit Scheme for Female Industrial Workers
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Female industrial workers/employees (maternity benefit)
schemes.eligibility: Female industrial worker/employee for at least six months before the delivery; benefit available twice in her lifetime.
schemes.benefit: Lumpsum grant of Rs.4000/- (Rupees Four Thousand Only) per delivery, paid by cheque/demand draft.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application in prescribed proforma (Annexure I) to the Secretary, Goa Labour Welfare Board within six months of delivery, with birth certificate of child, certificate of being an industrial worker (from employer or a Gazetted Officer), and certificate from medical officer (DHS/GMC/recognised gynaecologist) that benefit is claimed first/second time.
schemes.notes: Under Goa, Daman and Diu Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1986.

schemes.name: Scheme No. VII - Scheme for Organising Sports, Games, Social and Cultural Activities for Industrial Workers/Employees
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Industrial workers and families in areas with 1,000 or more industrial workers
schemes.eligibility: Events in areas where concentration of industrial workers is 1,000 or more; organised by the Board, managements, reputed social/cultural organisations or workers' recreation clubs.
schemes.benefit: For events arranged by management or voluntary organisation: reimbursement of 50% of cost subject to maximum Rs. 5,000/- per event; total annual expenditure for an area with 10,000 or more workers not to exceed Rs. 20,000/-.
schemes.how_to_apply: After the event, management/voluntary organisation submits claim to the Secretary with nature of event, participant list, original bills, stamped acquaintance, advance stamped receipt and detailed report; Board approval required.
schemes.notes: Rs. 5,000 is per event to organiser.

schemes.name: Scheme No. VIII - Scheme for Excursion-cum Study Tours for the Workers/Employees Employed at Various Industrial Establishments
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Industrial establishment managements organising study tours for workers
schemes.eligibility: Implemented through managements; one trip per establishment per financial year subject to funds; tour max 10 days and 3000 kms; 10 to 50 workers per trip. Workers (permanent or temporary) must be on wage register with at least two years continuous service, hold identity card, monthly earning not exceeding Rs. 2,600/-; preference to longer service and lesser pay; dependants not eligible; not eligible again for 4 years.
schemes.benefit: Grant-in-aid on matching basis up to maximum Rs. 20,000/- per tour: 50% bus hire charges (not exceeding second-class train fare cost); DA to workers Rs. 50/- per day per worker; emergent postal/telegram/telephone charges up to Rs. 200/- per tour; accident insurance premium up to Rs. 10/- per worker.
schemes.how_to_apply: Management submits proposal in Form 'A' to the Secretary; Advisory Committee approval; itinerary approved before tour; participant list with Form 'B' declarations 15 days before; management incurs expenditure and claims reimbursement with bills, participant list, DA acquaintance, receipt and tour report.
schemes.notes: Rs. 20,000 is per tour (to management), not per worker.

schemes.name: Scheme No. X - Scheme for Treatment of Mentally Challenged and Spastic Children of Industrial Workers
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Industrial workers with mentally challenged or spastic children fully dependent on parents
schemes.eligibility: Worker covered under Goa, Daman and Diu Labour Welfare Act, 1986 with at least six months continuous service, irrespective of pay limit; child certified as mentally challenged (Institute of Psychiatry) or spastic (Orthopaedic Surgeon/Physician of Asilo Hospital Mapusa, GMC Panaji or Hospicio Margao), certificate renewed yearly; subsistence allowance only where worker is the only earning member with no other source of income during child's treatment.
schemes.benefit: Subsistence allowance @ Rs. 3000/- p.m.
schemes.how_to_apply: Form 'A' to the Secretary, Goa Labour Welfare Board through employer, certified by competent medical authority, with manager attestation; yearly alive certificate signed before a Gazetted Officer.
schemes.notes: Amount is per month.

schemes.name: Scheme No. XI - Scheme for Grant-in-Aid to Libraries from Goa Labour Welfare Fund
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Employers maintaining libraries for workers and their dependents
schemes.eligibility: Employer maintaining a library for workers and dependents irrespective of trade union affiliation; library must serve a working population of at least two hundred and fifty workers; books per list approved by the Secretary; management willing to spend matching amount; bond to be executed.
schemes.benefit: Grant-in-aid per annum for purchase of books only, paid on matching basis on production of vouchers, restricted to Rs. 25,000/-.
schemes.how_to_apply: Prescribed application form and bond to the Secretary, Goa Labour Welfare Board.

schemes.name: Scheme No. XII - Scheme to Pay Incentives to the Wards of Workers on the Basis of Percentage of Marks Obtained by them on Passing Final Examination Conducted by the Boards/Universities from Class X Onwards
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Wards of workers/employees in Goa passing Board/University exams from Class X onwards
schemes.eligibility: Ward of worker/employee employed in Goa (parent with more than 6 months continuous service in establishment covered by Labour Welfare Fund Act, non-supervisory); passed final exam of Board/University from Class X onwards with First Division (60% above) or Second Division (50% above).
schemes.benefit: Incentive (1st Division / 2nd Division): High School (X) Rs. 1,250/- / Rs. 875/-; Plus 2/ITI (XI & XII) Rs. 1,875/- / Rs. 1,250/-; Graduation/3-year Prof. Diploma Rs. 2,500/- / Rs. 1,875/-; Prof. Degree (BE/MBBS/B.Arch. etc) Rs. 5,000/- / Rs. 3,750/-.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application (Annexure I) to Head of Educational Institution with attested marksheet and employer certificate (Annexure III); institution forwards with class-wise statement (Annexure II) to the Board within one month of result announcement.

schemes.name: Scheme No. XIII - Scheme for Payment of Extra Monetary Compensation for Sterilization to Employees
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Workers/employees or their spouses undergoing vasectomy/tubectomy
schemes.eligibility: Worker/employee or spouse with two or less living children who has undergone vasectomy/tubectomy at recognised hospital; payable only once in lifetime; claim within one year of operation; employer certificate of more than 6 months continuous service in establishment covered by Labour Welfare Fund Act.
schemes.benefit: Monetary incentive of Rs. 4,000/- per head, over and above incentives from other agencies.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application (Annexure B) with doctor's certificate (Annexure A) and employer certificate (Annexure C) to the Secretary, Goa Labour Welfare Board; statement of not more than two living children countersigned by Sarpanch of the Panchayat, Mamlatdar, a Gazetted Officer or authority notified by the Board.
schemes.notes: Sarpanch is only one of the alternative authorities to countersign the declaration.

schemes.name: Scheme No. XIV - Scheme for T.B. Domiciliary Treatment of Employees Covered under the Goa Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1986
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Industrial workers suffering from T.B. under domiciliary treatment, and their dependents
schemes.eligibility: Workers covered under the Act suffering from T.B. advised domiciliary treatment through approved dispensaries/State Government health centres; benefit for not more than nine months or until fitness certificate, whichever earlier. Subsistence allowance only where worker is the only earning member with no other income; not for a woman patient whose husband is working, nor where patient is a dependent of worker.
schemes.benefit: Medical treatment charges not exceeding Rs. 300/- p.m. (actual reasonable cost reimbursed); subsistence allowance to dependent up to maximum Rs. 1000/- p.m. where worker is sole earner, and Rs. 400/- p.m. where the dependents are more than one.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application form to Goa Labour Welfare Board with attestation by manager/owner and certificate of the medical officer.
schemes.notes: Amounts are per month. Subsistence allowance wording (Rs. 1000 vs Rs. 400 when dependents more than one) is as printed and appears ambiguous.

schemes.name: Scheme No. XVI - Labour Welfare Centres: Scheme for the Benefits of Children of Industrial Workers/Employees
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Children of industrial workers/employees (training in embroidery, cutting and tailoring)
schemes.eligibility: Admission restricted to children of industrial workers/employees; children of Government servants including teachers in Government and private schools admitted on merit of case; no age limit; trainees with contagious diseases not admitted.
schemes.benefit: Training at Labour Welfare Centres (embroidery, cutting and tailoring) in morning (9.30 am-1.15 pm) and evening (2.00-5.45 pm) batches, with examinations.
schemes.notes: Mainly describes modalities of operating centres; no fees or monetary benefit stated.

schemes.name: Scheme No. XVII - Retrenched Workers Assistance Scheme
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Retrenched workmen and workmen affected by closure
schemes.eligibility: At least 4 years continuous service (service of min. 4 years in more than one company allowed, burden of proof on workman); not eligible on completing age 58; not if resigned, abandoned service or availed VRS; benefit ceases on gainful employment (undertaking to disclose); Social Security Card under Goa Employment (Condition of Service) and Retirement Benefits Act, 2001 desirable; approval by Board or its Committee.
schemes.benefit: Monthly assistance: up to age 40 Rs. 3000/- per month; 41-50 years Rs. 4000/- per month; above 51 to 58 years Rs. 5000/- per month; duration up to one year from retrenchment for minimum 4 years service, plus two months for every additional year above 4 years, maximum 30 months.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application (Annexure I) to Goa Labour Welfare Board with age proof (birth/baptism/school leaving certificate), appointment letter/wage slip, employer certificate of emoluments, and retrenchment notice.
schemes.valid_period: Retrospectively effective from 01-04-2003
schemes.notes: Max benefit is per month. Funding source not explicitly stated (Board scheme).

schemes.name: Scheme No. XVIII - Scheme to Grant Financial Assistance to Laid Off Workman
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Laid-off workmen in industrial establishments
schemes.eligibility: Employed in industrial establishment covered under Chapter V-A and V-B of Industrial Disputes Act, 1947; minimum 45 days lay-off; at least one year continuous service (service in more than one company allowed, burden of proof on workman); not eligible after age 58; not if resigned, abandoned service or availed VRS; benefit ceases on gainful employment; Social Security Card under Goa Employment (Condition of Service) and Retirement Benefit Act, 2001 desirable; approval by Board committee.
schemes.benefit: Monthly assistance based on wages (basic+DA+VDA): up to Rs. 10,000/- -> Rs. 3,000/- p.m.; Rs.5000/- to Rs.15,000/- -> Rs. 4,000/- p.m.; Rs.15,001/- to Rs.20,000/- -> Rs. 5,000/- p.m.; Rs.20,001/- to Rs.25,000/- -> Rs. 6,000/- p.m.; Rs.25,001/- and above -> Rs. 7,000/- p.m.; initially for 45 days, extendable on review to maximum 90 days.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application (Annexure I) to the Secretary, Goa Labour Welfare Board, supported by appointment letter/wage slip, employer certificate of emoluments, and lay-off notice.
schemes.notes: Max benefit is per month. Text says scheme 'shall be financed by the Government'. Wage slabs overlap as printed (a) up to Rs. 10,000 and (b) Rs. 5000 to Rs. 15,000.

schemes.name: Scheme XV - Scheme to Provide Incentive / Financial Assistance on the Attendance in Schools/Colleges etc. to the Female Students Studying in Classes V and Onwards being Daughters of Workers/Employees
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Daughters of workers/employees (incl. contract labourers) studying in Class V onwards
schemes.eligibility: Female students, daughters of employees/workers (including contract labourers) covered under Goa Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1986, studying in Government recognised schools/colleges/universities in Class V onwards; either parent a worker for at least six months; family income from all sources (father, mother, unmarried siblings) not exceeding Rs. 20,000/- p.m.; daughters of supervisory staff not eligible; once per class; other similar incentives reduce award to the excess.
schemes.benefit: Rs. 10/- per day of attendance, subject to maximum ceiling of Rs. 2400/- per annum per child; paid once a year via ECS to parents' bank account; in addition to existing scholarships.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application (Annexure I, plain paper/newspaper cutting/printed form acceptable) authenticated by Head of Institution and employer certificate, to the Secretary, Goa Labour Welfare Board by 30th September.

schemes.name: Stri Sakhi Scheme (Scheme No. XIX - Scheme to Install Sanitary Napkin Vending Machine and Incinerators in Industrial Units and Schools/Colleges)
schemes.department: Office Of The Commissioner, Labour and Employment
schemes.target: Female industrial workers and their daughters studying from class VII onwards
schemes.eligibility: Industrial units/establishments (preferably with high concentration of women workers) and Government schools/colleges where workers' children study; management must provide suitable place (preferably washroom), sign MoU with the Board, maintain and replenish machine; not more than one machine per industrial establishment.
schemes.benefit: Board procures and installs one sanitary napkin vending machine (Re.1 coin operated) and one incinerator; Board bears cost of installation and replenishment for schools/colleges and locations serving a cluster of small industrial units; in other units employer replenishes using coin collections.
schemes.how_to_apply: Application form (in duplicate) signed by owner/manager/principal/headmistress to Goa Labour Welfare Board.
schemes.valid_period: Comes into force with immediate effect
schemes.notes: In-kind benefit; no rupee amounts for machines stated.

schemes.name: Deen Dayal Swasthya Seva Yojana (DDSSY) - auto renewal of card with blanket cover 01-04-2022 to 31-03-2023

schemes.name: Chief Minister's Rojgar Yojana 2020 for Engineering Professionals
schemes.target: Young Diploma/Degree engineers (Civil/Electrical/Mechanical) in Goa seeking self-employment
schemes.eligibility: Engineering professionals in Goa seeking self-employment and assistance for execution of PWD projects; age restricted to 35 years, relaxable by 5 years for physically challenged, SC, ST and OBC; Degree/Diploma in Civil/Electrical/Mechanical Engineering (Civil degree/diploma for Water supply & waste water, Building, Roads/Bridges/land development works; relevant-field degree/diploma for Electrical & Mechanical works); permanent resident of Goa for at least 15 years (Residential Certificate from Mamlatdar); not an existing enlisted contractor/partner/director of firm enlisted with PWD (affidavit); not a defaulter to any Nationalized Bank/Financial Institution/Co-operative Bank; income of applicant with spouse, dependents and minor children not to exceed Rs. 10,00,000/- p.a.; person already assisted under other subsidy linked scheme not eligible unless relaxed/specified.
schemes.benefit: Award of PWD project contracts on limited e-tender basis among engineers empanelled under the scheme: fresh Diploma/Degree holders eligible to quote for works up to Rs. 5.00 lakhs (Class V); Degree/Diploma engineers with 5 years experience eligible for works up to Rs. 10.00 lakhs (Class IV). Only one work at a time; maximum four works then exit; not more than two works in a financial year. EMD maximum Rs. 500.00 (Class V) and Rs. 1000.00 (Class IV); for physically challenged/SC/ST/OBC maximum Rs. 250.00 (Class V) and Rs. 500.00 (Class IV); no performance guarantee, security deposit @ 2.5% of bill amount withheld till end of maintenance period; tender form cost maximum Rs. 200.00. Training in tender preparation, tender process and e-tender procedure. On exit, eligible for enlistment as contractor in respective categories.
schemes.how_to_apply: Submit application in prescribed form (Annexure I) to the enlistment authority with supporting documents: Undertaking (Annexure II) on Rs. 100 stamp paper before Executive Magistrate/Notary, self-attested Degree/Diploma certificate, experience certificate (if any), identity and residential proof, Residential Certificate issued by Mamlatdar. Task Force Committees scrutinize applications; Engineering Officer, PWD is Nodal Officer.
schemes.valid_period: Comes into force from date of publication in Official Gazette
schemes.notes: Official Gazette Series I No. 37 dated 10-12-2020; order signed Panaji 4th December 2020. Heavy OCR damage; the Rs. 5 lakh/Rs. 10 lakh contract limits are works ceilings, not cash benefits, so max_benefit_inr left null. Residency years partly illegible in rules text; 15 years taken from Annexure II undertaking. Applicant must arrange own working capital, manpower, plant and machinery. Gazette also contains an unrelated TCP heritage-list notification and draft Municipalities rules (not schemes).

schemes.name: CMRY Scheme 2020 (Chief Minister's Rojgar Yojana 2020) - Application for Enlistment and Annexures
schemes.target: Civil/Mechanical/Electrical Degree/Diploma engineers seeking enlistment under CMRY 2020
schemes.eligibility: Per undertaking and checklist: age restricted to 35 years (relaxable by 5 years for PD/SC/ST/OBC); Degree/Diploma in Civil/Mechanical/Electrical Engineering; permanent resident of Goa for last fifteen years (Residential Certificate from Mamlatdar, minimum 15 years); not registered as contractor in individual capacity in Goa PWD; not black-listed/banned; not a member of Parliament or State Legislature; not partner/director of another firm registered with PWD as contractor; no civil or criminal case pending; not a defaulter to any bank/financial institution; not availed assistance under any other subsidy linked scheme of Government; income with spouse, dependents and minor children not exceeding Rs. 1000000/- per annum.
schemes.benefit: Enlistment under CMRY 2020 scheme (benefits defined in the scheme notification; not stated in this document).
schemes.how_to_apply: Application for Enlistment (Annexure I) with: Undertaking Annexure II on Rs 100 stamp paper executed before Executive Magistrate or Notary; self-attested PAN and Aadhar card; self-attested birth certificate; Residential Certificate from Mamlatdar; self-attested Degree/Diploma certificate; experience certificate if any. Assistance from taluka-wise PWD Nodal Officers (Executive Engineers, Annexure III) or PWD Head Office, Altinho, Panaji (Engineering Officer).
schemes.notes: Document is the application form, undertaking, taluka nodal officer list and document checklist for CMRY 2020; not the scheme rules themselves (see doc 4d1ffbbf26). Applicant must arrange working capital, manpower, plant and machinery.

schemes.name: Subsidized scheme with a one time payment as sewerage connection charges
schemes.department: Sewerage and Infrastructural Development Corporation of Goa Ltd
schemes.target: Domestic and other consumers availing mandatory sewer connection where Government sewerage facility is available
schemes.eligibility: Existing domestic consumers (houses, apartments, etc.) and new consumers (new constructions) in areas where sewerage facility is made available by Government; BPL families get concessional rate.
schemes.benefit: One-time sewerage connection fees with application. Existing domestic consumers: individual houses & bungalows Rs. 5000/- each; BPL families Rs. 100/Unit; group houses/multiple housing units Rs. 3000/- per each flat; shops with toilet/water connections Rs. 2000/- per each; shops without toilet/water connections Rs. 1000/- per each. New consumers: individual houses & bungalows Rs. 9500/each unit; BPL families Rs. 100/Unit; co-operative housing societies (registered or not) Rs. 5500/each flat or unit; student hostels/hospitals/dispensaries/educational institutions/charitable trusts Rs. 9500/each unit; other hostels/hospitals/Government offices/autonomous bodies etc. Rs. 9500/each unit; small hotels, bars & restaurants (<15 rooms)/non-AC Government tourist hostels up to 150 sq. mts. Rs. 5500/each unit; commercial/cinema/malls/supermarkets/hotels Rs. 25000/each unit. Monthly sewerage charges 35% of Water Consumption Bill (50% for small hotels and commercial categories).
schemes.how_to_apply: Connection fee payable with application for sewer connection.
schemes.notes: Notification No. 8-4/PCE-PWD-Accts/2020-21/07 issued by PWD (Principal Chief Engineer), Official Gazette Series I No. 5 dated 29-04-2021. Subsidy amount itself not stated; figures are fees payable, so max_benefit_inr null. Categories 3 to 6 of new consumers also bear actual cost of house sewer connection. Monthly charges replace those of Notification dated 12-05-2020. Linked companion notification (same date) amends Goa Sewerage System and Sanitation Services Management Rules, 2010 making connection mandatory within two months within 100 mts with penalties of 25%/50% of water charges. Gazette issue also contains unrelated items (Co-operative Societies draft rules, police posts, Covid private hospital rates).

schemes.name: Kamdhenu Scheme (Sudharit) Amended 2021
schemes.department: Department Of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services
schemes.target: Dairy farmers / youth setting up dairy units
schemes.eligibility: Bonafide resident of Goa for at least 05 years; pucca cattle shed with cement flooring; undertake to strictly stall feed (no open grazing); new applicants must undergo dairy training at designated centre (old traditional dairy farmers with crossbred/improved/indigenous animals who had not availed Kamdhenu may be exempted on Area Officer recommendation); knowledge or experience in cattle/buffalo farming or trained by Department; land for green fodder cultivation desirable; farmer who had availed the purchase of animals under the earlier Kamdhenu Scheme (listed under eligibility); must have cattle shed; be member of local Dairy Society/Bachat Gat/SHG (those branding own dairy products may be permitted without membership); letter from financing institution having ECS willing to finance.
schemes.benefit: Unit cost of Cross Bred Cow/Improved She Buffalo/Indigenous breed cow (Sahiwal, Gir, Red Sindhi, Rathi, Tharparkar) limited to Rs. 70,000/- per animal. Subsidy on cost of animal: 1 to 10 animals 90% (Rs. 63000), 11 to 20 animals 75% (Rs. 52500), 21 to 100 animals 50% (Rs. 35000), all categories; credited via ECS to financing institution/beneficiary account. Transport incentive Rs. 2000/- per animal (or actual, whichever less) for purchase outside the state; Rs. 800/- per animal (or actual, whichever less) for purchase at cattle melas organized by the Department. If animal dies within one month of purchase (not due to negligence), cost of animal credited to beneficiary.
schemes.how_to_apply: Documents include: consent for Aadhaar seeding/authentication; affidavit in prescribed format re ownership of cattle shed and Form I & XIV; caste certificate of SC/ST/Dhangar (if applicable); letter from financing institution with ECS; passport size photograph; residence verified/attested by local area Officer. Animals to be purchased within one year of sanction, from Department cattle melas or outside the state (outside-state purchase needs prior written permission and minimum 10 animals at a time).
schemes.notes: max_benefit_inr is the subsidy per animal (1-10 animal slab); total per beneficiary not stated (up to 100 animals). notified_on is the Gazette issue date (Series I No. 29); corrigendum 926aced651 gives notification date as 04-10-2021. Animals must be insured (comprehensive, min 3½ years) and microchipped/ear-tagged. Trimmed: details may be on later pages.

schemes.name: Pashupalan Scheme (Amended)
schemes.department: Department Of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services
schemes.target: Owners of non-descript cattle/buffalo and cross-bred/improved/indigenous female calves; NGOs, Goshalas, community farms
schemes.eligibility: All farmers availing Artificial Insemination facility for cattle and buffalo and registered with local Government Veterinary Services; NGOs, Goshalas, Community Farms and other organizations availing A.I.; all farmers irrespective of financial status; farmers having cross-bred/improved buffalo/indigenous (Sahiwal, Gir, Red Sindhi) female calves born of A.I., born to existing animals, or bought under Kamdhenu/Western Ghat/Modern Dairy or other Government schemes. Animals must be stall-fed/tied; calves must gain at least 30 kg per quarter (min 30 kg at 3 months).
schemes.benefit: Phase 1: incentive Rs. 500/- for 1st A.I. and Rs. 200/- for 2nd A.I. of non-descript cow/buffalo. Phase 2: on confirmation of pregnancy, Rs. 2,000/- per month for feed, fodder & misc. from 4th month onward. Phase 3: Rs. 4,000/- on birth of female cross-bred/improved buffalo calf to local cow/buffalo; calf feed allowance from birth to 27 months at 75% of estimated expenditure (quarterly subsidy Rs. 5,625/-, 2,625/-, 3,375/-, 3,375/-, 4,800/- x4, 5,400/-); 100% subsidy for S.C./S.T. & Dhangar community.
schemes.how_to_apply: Register animals at local Veterinary Dispensary/Hospital (Forms I-V); submit caste certificate if SC/ST/Dhangar and bank passbook copy (account no., MICR, IFSC); Area VO/AD submits records and quarterly weight-gain certificates (Annexure A) to Head Office; subsidy credited to bank account.
schemes.notes: Notification No. 14-55/AHVS/16-17/1041; notified_on is Gazette issue date (Series I No. 10). Monthly feed incentive is Rs. 2,000 per month; amounts are per A.I./per animal/per quarter and no single per-beneficiary total is stated, so max_benefit_inr left null (estimated rearing cost Rs. 52,800 per calf). Trimmed: details may be on later pages.

schemes.name: Financial Assistance for Medical Treatment for infertility amongst Scheduled Tribe couples by IVF (Invitro Fertilization) & IUI (Intra Uterine Insemination) Method under Matrutva Yojana
schemes.target: Scheduled Tribe couples with infertility and no living issue
schemes.eligibility: Couples/Husband or Wife belonging to Scheduled Tribes; no income limit; only in cases of infertility and couple having no living issue (couples without children even after 3 years of marriage due to primary infertility or other medical reasons); benefit for birth of first born child; treatment at Government Hospitals or empanelled Private Hospitals/Nursing Homes in Goa.
schemes.benefit: Financial assistance upto Rs. 5.00 Lakh for IVF or IUI treatment covering actual cost incl. diagnostic investigation, medicine, hospital admission, investigations needing admission or medical reasons during pregnancy, specialist fees, procedures like Laparoscopy, and delivery of baby. Unspent sanctioned amount may be used for delivery charges (restricted to Rs. 5.00 lakhs); expenditure above Rs. 5.00 Lakhs borne by beneficiary. Rates: one cycle IVF with medicine Rs. 1.00 lakh; one cycle IUI with medicine Rs. 15,000/-; Embryo Transfer Rs. 30,000/-; Embryo Freezing Rs. 30,000/-; Histroscopic Diagnostics Rs. 20,000/-; Laparoscopy Rs. 30,000 to Rs. 80,000/- (rates maintained two years, reviewed for medical inflation). Paid to empanelled hospital via Goa Scheduled Tribe Finance and Development Corporation.
schemes.how_to_apply: Submit filled application form to Directorate of Tribal Welfare with: copy of provisional ST certificate (Dy. Collector or competent authority; mandatory), Marriage Certificate, Aadhar Card copy of couple, Birth Certificate, any medical papers. Empanelled hospitals/applicants submit doctor-certified bills to Directorate of Tribal Welfare.
schemes.notes: Amends clauses 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9 and 15; other clauses unchanged. Also covers hospital empanelment criteria (18-24 months IUI/IVF experience, 25% success rate, empanelment for 5 years) and Monitoring Committee. Comes into force from date of publication (OG Series I No. 24 dated 09-09-2021). Gazette issue also contains PWD water tariff revision (free water up to 16m3/month) - not a scheme row.

schemes.eligibility: Any person residing in Goa for at least 05 years; pucca cattle shed with cement flooring; undertake strict stall feeding (no open grazing); new entrants must undergo two weeks practical training on Government Farms; knowledge or experience in cattle/buffalo farming; land for green fodder desirable; farmer who availed purchase under earlier Kamdhenu Scheme (listed under eligibility); letter from financing institution with ECS willing to finance; purchase within one year of sanction.
